jobs.title: Site Operations Manager
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Site Operations Manager to lead the deployment and operation of autonomous construction technology on partner construction sites. This role is responsible for ensuring successful site launches, safe operational performance, and strong partner relationships from early planning through project completion.

This role goes beyond traditional site operations—it includes the end-to-end customer operational experience, including hands-on customer training to operate autonomous systems and ongoing operations throughout the lifecycle of the project.

The Site Operations Manager acts as the operational point of contact for the partner site project management, while coordinating closely with engineering, partnership, and operations teams to deliver safe, efficient, and high-quality site operations.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Deployment & Site Operations

 - Contribute to early-stage site assessments and operational feasibility reviews.

 - Define work plans including scope and operational requirements.

 - Plan and execute deployments across multiple partner sites

 - Coordinate onsite launch readiness across engineering, fleet, and site teams

 - Lead onsite setup, workflow validation, and safety alignment

 - Own site launch and transition into steady-state operations

 - Oversee daily operations to ensure safe, reliable performance

 - Run regular operational check-ins with partners

 - Capture field insights to inform product, engineering and operational improvements

 - Manage project closeout, reporting, and post-deployment learnings





Customer Robot Operation Experience

 - Manage the customer lifecycle from launch through steady-state operations.

 - Lead structured training and support for new partners, ensuring alignment on workflows, expectations, safety and success criteria.

 - Translate complex robotic systems into clear, practical operating instructions.

 - Certify that partner site management and operators are fully trained and confident prior to and after launch.

 - Partner with internal stakeholders to incorporate field learnings into training materials and workflows.

 - Build strong, trust-based relationships with partner teams to drive long-term success and adoption.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Safe, on-time deployment of autonomous operations

 - Customer teams independently operating robotic systems with confidence

 - Strong onboarding experience with fast time-to-productivity

 - High customer satisfaction driven by training, support, and engagement

 - Strong partner relationships and clear communication

 - Continuous improvement of partner training and deployment processes




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - Experience managing operations in construction or industrial environments

 - Experience directing and coordinating heavy equipment operators and field crews

 - Ability to interpret site construction drawings, site maps, survey data, and grading plans to support earthwork operations

 - Experience leading cross-functional initiatives with engineering and field teams

 - Excellent communication and partner management skills

 - Experience training customers and customer support in an operational setting

 - Comfortable working in dynamic, fast-changing environments

 - Knowledge of OSHA regulations and construction safety best practices, with experience ensuring compliance in the field

 - Willingness to travel 50%+ and work from customer sites

Located in surrounding Austin area

Preferred

 - Background in autonomy, robotics, or advanced construction technology

 - Familiarity with construction tool Propeller Aero

 - Experience launching new operational programs or deployments

 - Experience building training programs, manuals, or playbooks

 - Familiarity with customer-facing tools or operational platforms




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

This role is critical not just for deploying technology, but for ensuring customers can successfully adopt, operate, and scale it. Your ability to train, onboard, and support partner teams will directly determine deployment success and long-term growth.





Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

jobs.title: Construction Business Development
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ROLE OVERVIEW

The commercial team owns our partner relationships, helping us find the right job sites for data collection and autonomy, and importantly bringing design partner construction expertise and feedback into the company so that our product managers, operations and engineers can take that feedback and build it into our product roadmap and execution.


This is a construction-native business development role focused on general contractors and earthwork subcontractors. You will help us find and partner with the right early partners, owning these relationships fully: sourcing, qualifying, closing, growing: coordinating deployment, and managing the ongoing relationship as our technology and commercial model mature.

You will build real relationships through in-person and virtual interactions, continuing to keep the bar of service high - building relationships with partners in the field and at the executive level.

This hire brings deep construction experience and know-how to the commercial team. 

The ideal candidate could reside in San Francisco, Austin, Texas or be remote. 

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own and execute the GC and earthwork-sub design partner relationships. Identify, engage, qualify, and close partnerships – end-to-end through the pipeline.

 - Spend real time on active job sites scope earthwork, read the work, and build trust with the people running it

 - Build deep, trusted relationships across every level, weighted toward the field: superintendents, foremen, operators, and equipment managers, through PMs and executives

 - Navigate GC procurement, subcontracting structures, licensing, and COI requirements to get machines mobilized

 - Act as the bridge between partners and our internal product, operations, and engineering teams carrying field reality back into the roadmap

 - Help refine our ideal customer profile, segmentation, and partner prioritization based on what you learn in the field

 - Maintain a well-organized pipeline with forecasting discipline and clear reporting

 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

Required

 - 10+ years in construction, earthwork, or heavy civil; very comfortable on a dynamic job site with field credibility, especially around the earthwork scope comfortable holding substantive conversations with supers, foreman, operators and equipment managers; scope work in the field, and talk schedule and production realistically

 - 2+ years working closely with construction technology either selling/deploying it, or as the GC/sub-side buyer or champion who rolled it out

 - Has substantial experience in business development; managing a quota and pipeline in various stages of a deal cycle with ability to sell, maintain and grow partners

 - Clear track record of exceeding goals / finding ways to get things done fast and in the right way

 - Deep familiarity with GC procurement and subcontracting structures how sites get bid, awarded, and mobilized

 - Adaptability and grit, comfortable in early-stage ambiguity with no established playbook

 - Low ego, high ownership, rolls up sleeves, finds creative solutions, does what it takes without being asked

 - Willing to travel heavily to active sites and partner HQs

Nice to Have

 - Track record landing and growing accounts with General Contractors and/or earthwork subs

 - Experience bringing skeptical field teams from doubt to active adoption of new tech or equipment

 - Familiarity with OEM, dealer, or rental partnership models

 - Experience scaling from early pilots to multi-site or fleet-wide deployments

 - Prior experience at a venture-backed or high-growth technology company

jobs.title: Data Operations Lead
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.



ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Data Operations Lead to own ongoing data collection support for the fleet - ensuring machines in the field reliably produce, retain, and deliver terabyte-scale daily data volumes.  Over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform. You will be the single-threaded owner to define our data collection strategies as well as oversee execution.  You will help define how the data is collected, when the data is collected, and the data center strategy for supporting efficient upload.  You will provide the critical data our Engineering teams rely on, including helping to define service level agreements and methods, monitoring, and infrastructure needs.

This is a field-forward leadership role. You will build the organization and the systems that keep data flowing, ensuring our engineering team has what they need in an efficient and economic method.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own ongoing data collection support for the fleet ensuring machines in the field reliably produce, retain, and deliver the terabyte-scale daily data volumes Engineering depends on.

 - Own field operations across Autonomous and Bedrock Intelligence machines at customer and engineering product standards: higher monitoring frequency, faster response, and stricter data completeness than the data collection fleet, because customers are paying for and acting on what these machines produce.

 - Own field operations across Data Collection machines at engineering product standards: define efficient means of data collection that still enable engineers with the critical data they need to mature our models.

 - Own data yield as a first-class operational metric alongside machine uptime: what percentage of operating hours produce usable, complete, correctly-labeled data, and what is driving the gap.   Work with engineering and product to prioritize and close places where data loss happens in the pipeline.

 - Build an overall economic service by ensuring SLAs are clear and costs understood, run simulations to better understand network strategy and SLA trade-offs and to optimize operations.

 - Own the field-side reliability of the data pipeline offload, connectivity, storage, and handoff and the operating cadence that catches degradation before Engineering or a paying customer discovers it downstream.

 - Translate Engineering, ML, and Bedrock Intelligence product requirements into field-executable standards, and translate field constraints back into realistic commitments.

 - Partner with Infrastructure, Product, Engineering and Data teams on tooling, instrumentation, and the roadmap for reducing manual effort in data operations as fleet size grows.

 - Work with IT to define the data center needs for efficient data upload and the playbook to bring a new data center online for data offload purposes.

 - Define labor and 3rd party strategies to execute data collection.  Monitor and continuously improve performance.



Team Leadership

 - Own data operations org design, labor strategies, and hiring and development for data technicians and couriers.

 - Build strong relationships with 3rd party service partners and oversee performance to specifications.

 - Be the bridge between active operations in the field and internal engineering teams that are customers of the data.

 - Build strong relationships with Customers as needed and ensure Bedrock employees and representatives comply with all active site rules and requirements.



WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Strong data yield per machine-hour and pipeline reliability

 - Lower cost per machine-hour and higher utilization.

 - Defined data center footprint enabling economic rapid scaling

 - High employee and Customer satisfaction; compliance to all Customer Site requirements

 - Robust Partner relationships, measured through business outcomes and performance

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 8-10 years in operations, field deployment, or program leadership, including 3+ years working with distributed teams across multiple sites or regions.

 - Experience working with non-exempt employees and experience either directly managing non-exempt employees or overseeing contingent staff.

 - Track record owning operational metrics for a physical fleet at scale, including SLA design and vendor performance management.

 - Experience running operations for a customer-facing product against committed SLAs, or an equivalent paid-service operation.

 - Experience partnering with Engineering or Product as the operational voice in platform and roadmap decisions.

 - Comfort in an early-stage environment where the playbook is written in real time, paired with the discipline to write it down.

 - Strong written and verbal communication with customer executives, dealer partners, and internal leadership.

 - Willingness to travel approximately 30% to job sites, dealer facilities, and partner locations.

Preferred

 - Background in autonomy, machine control, telematics, or connected fleet solutions.

 - Experience operating working with a data collection fleet or equivalent field data infrastructure.

 - Experience structuring in-house versus third-party service decisions and the contractual and performance frameworks behind them.

 - Established relationships with large general contractors, hyperscaler builders, or heavy civil customers.

 - Understanding of data center requirements for data offload.

 - Experience working through a platform generation transition and/ or the introduction of new machine/equipment types.

WORKING CONDITIONS

This is a field-forward role with regular presence at active job sites, dealer and upfit facilities, and Bedrock offices. Travel is approximately 30%, concentrated during site bring-up, data center bring ups, and service partner engagements.

jobs.title: Head of Operations Planning and Special Projects
jobs.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING ADVANCED AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and into the real world. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. Today, we're deploying autonomous systems on heavy construction equipment across the country, improving safety on job sites and accelerating schedules on critical infrastructure projects.

We're not here debating the future of AI. We're deploying it in the real world. In just two years, we've raised $350M and achieved the first fully autonomous excavator deployments in construction.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Bedrock's technology is scaling rapidly —over the next twelve months, we will rapidly scale our machine count, partners, and sites while also adding net-new machine types and a next-generation platform.  

The Head of Operations Planning & Special Projects owns aligning cross-functionally on an integrated machine plan across types, generations, product lines, partners, sites in order to develop Operational headcount and material plans; ultimately, giving the business a clear view of what's required and by when. 

You'll own the integrated machine plan, scenario planning, cross-functional alignment when constraints arise, building headcount scaling factors and plans, and standing up our early Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process. Reporting to the VP of Operations, you'll be a critical thought partner to the VP and each Operations Lead.


WHAT YOU'LL DO


INTEGRATED PLANNING

 - Own the integrated operations plan covering requirements across all product lines, machines, field headcount, and material readiness.

 - Identify constraints in the plan and build scenarios that drive resolution or acceptable alternatives.

 - Partner with each Operations leader to surface optimizations, risks, and constraints, and develop paths to mitigation.

 - Support senior leadership and board-level decisions with clear, rigorous analysis.

 - Partner with the VP of Operations to define team OKRs, the mechanisms to track them, and routine reporting on critical initiatives.

 - Contribute to the long-term forecast, integrating priorities across multiple teams.

 - Help align data collection needs with operational optimizations to strengthen our data pipelines.


S&OP PROCESS IMPLEMENTATION

 - Partner with Commercial, Finance, Supply Chain, Engineering, and Operations to build stage-appropriate S&OP processes that tee up critical business decisions, surface constraints, and evaluate alternatives.

 - Own the monthly S&OP cycle end to end: forecast development, demand review inputs, forecast analysis, supply plan integration, pre-meeting coordination, and reporting.

 - Forecast demand, assess whether projected supply can meet it, and define key performance metrics such as forecast accuracy and fulfillment rate.

 - Serve as the bridge between business strategy, engineering build plans, finance, and supply chain execution.


PRODUCTION PLANNING COORDINATION

 - Own phase-in / phase-out planning for new machine types, product lines, partners and sites, and hardware generations — including availability, supply constraints, retrofits, and partner transitions.

 - Track lead times and drive alignment on critical decision timelines and order dates.

 - Work with Operations leaders to plan labor availability, using key ratios and operational planning drivers.

 - Partner with Supply Chain and Contract Manufacturing to plan production capacity against demand, consolidate risks, and drive prioritization when supply is constrained.


OPERATIONS INSIGHTS & ANALYTICS

 - Own the development of core operational metrics and routine reporting.

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to the business.

 - Support continuous improvement across Operations through process and data.


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - A single, trusted integrated plan that the business uses to make decisions about machines, people, and materials.

 - Constraints surfaced early, with clear scenarios and recommendations — not surprises.

 - A functioning monthly S&OP cadence with consistent participation and clear decisions.

 - Core operational metrics defined, tracked, and reviewed on a regular rhythm.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


REQUIRED

 - 8–10 years in operations, planning, or program leadership, including 5+ years working with cross-functional teams distributed across sites or regions.

 - Demonstrated ability to influence leaders — aligning cross-functional stakeholders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth.

 - Track record implementing S&OP or supply-and-demand processes that bring clarity to requirements, decisions, and success criteria.

 - Experience planning and managing hourly / field workforce headcount.

 - Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to turn data into operational decisions.

 - Strong written and verbal communication, including with executives.


PREFERRED

 - Familiarity with autonomy, heavy machinery, and/or the construction industry.

 - Experience standing up supply-and-demand review processes that clarify timelines, requirements, decisions, risks, and solutions.

 - Continuous improvement, Lean, or Six Sigma experience, including standing up an improvement program.


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

As Bedrock scales, the hardest problems are increasingly about coordination: getting the right machines, people, and parts to the right sites at the right time. This role builds the planning backbone that lets every Operations team — and the company — make faster, better decisions with confidence.
